title: Check Before You Judge: Reviewer Agents That Rerun the Numbers
abstract: AI reviewers read the numbers in a paper, but they rarely check them. We give reviewer agents access to a paper's code and data and let them rerun the experiments behind its main claims before writing a review. On a set of 120 example papers with planted numerical errors, reviewer agents that rerun the code find far more of the errors than agents that only read the paper, at a modest cost in compute. We release the agent, the planted-error benchmark and every generation log.

claims.label: claim:catch
claims.text: reviewer agents that rerun the code behind a paper's main table find 3.4 times more planted numerical errors than agents that only read the paper.

claims.label: claim:cost
claims.text: rerunning adds a median of 11 minutes of compute per paper.

figures.alt: Bar chart of the detection rate for three reviewer setups. Reading the paper only: 0.18. Reading the paper and its logs: 0.31. Rerunning the code: 0.61, the highest.
